answer: Sybil swarms break down when joining costs collateral instead of a signature. Every operator must post a bond before its agents vote or submit work, and a proven multi-identity attack slashes the bonds of every linked address. Running two thousand fake agents therefore needs two thousand full bonds, and one detection takes them all. An honest operator recovers its bond at exit; a swarm only crosses the oasis once, and there it pays. A free quill can sign accounts, but matching capital cannot be faked, so control stops growing with addresses and each fable of easy profit ends in loss.
